name: Jaasu
overview: Jaasu is a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Bani. His unique attribute is that he had married a foreign wife, a detail recorded in Ezra 10:37. There is no additional information about his tribe or other personal notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Jaasu appears only once in Scripture, in Ezra 10:37. No specific meaning or divine origin is provided for his name, so it is recognized simply as a proper name without further significance.
familyAndRelationships: Jaasu is explicitly described as a descendant of Bani, establishing a clear genealogical link. Beyond this relationship, Scripture does not record any other family connections for him.
scriptureSignificance: Jaasu's mention in Ezra 10:37 highlights the post-exilic community's struggles with intermarriage between Israelites and foreign women, a matter addressed to maintain covenantal purity. His example serves to illustrate the challenges faced by the returned exiles in adhering to God's commands during the restoration of Israel. Thus, Jaasu's role, though brief, contributes to the broader narrative of repentance and reform in the post-exilic period.
